takeaway: Transitional cell carcinoma of the urinary tract: smoking causes about half; chemicals such as petroleum, paints and pigments (aniline dyes) and chronic irritation also predispose.

lines.text: Which carcinogen is linked to transitional cell carcinoma of the urinary tract?
Cigarette smoking contributes about one half of the disease burden.
Chemical exposure also predisposes to it: petroleum, paints and pigments,
As with most epithelial cancers, physical irritation also raises the risk of malignant change:
chronic urinary stones, chronic catheterization and chronic infection.
So the answer is aniline dyes.
